title: Reword a line the voice model refuses
statement: When a voice generator falsely refuses a line, find the refused sentence by trying sentences one at a time, reword it in print and voice, and never ship silence.
example: One batch of lessons met 2 false refusals of harmless instruction lines, each found by trying sentences one at a time.
detail: The reading course renderer's invariants for new lessons require every new clip to be listen-checked, and say a false prohibited-content refusal must be rephrased and retried, never shipped as silence (`grade3-reading/course-renderer/docs/qa/new-lesson-qa-invariants.md`, lines 126-131). In one batch of lessons from September 2026 the voice model refused two harmless instruction lines, 'Use them in your answer if you can.' and 'Choose all that fit.' (`grade3-reading/course-renderer/authoring/peter-pan/fill/l5-l7-parity/batch-2026-09-18/DECISIONS.md`, lines 11-12 and 57). Each was found by trying the sentences one at a time and reworded in the printed and the spoken copy alike, as 'Bring those clues into your answer if you can.' and 'Tap every one that fits.'

evidence.quote: **D7. Listen-check every new clip**: false PROHIBITED_CONTENT refusals must be rephrased and retried (never ship silence); watch for elision ("Rat"→"Rot", "The So row"→"the sorrow").
TTS refused "Use them in your answer if you can." (PROHIBITED_CONTENT, stable; per-sentence bisect `tmp/bisect-l6-p16.py`) → "Bring those clues into your answer if you can." printed + spoken
Second TTS refusal, bisected: "Choose all that fit." (L5 p18, L6 p17 msq stems) → "Tap every one that fits." printed + spoken.
